subject: general
question: Dhamma is the ________ word for the Sanskrit word 'Dharma'.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dhamma** is the Pali term for the Sanskrit word **Dharma**.
 
• Pali is an ancient language of the Indian subcontinent, primarily used in the scriptures of Theravada Buddhism.
 
• The **Tipitaka**, the sacred canon of Theravada Buddhism, is composed in Pali.
 
• Dhamma in Pali and Dharma in Sanskrit generally mean the teachings of the Buddha or the universal law.
 
• Pali language played a crucial role in the spread of Buddhism across South and Southeast Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pali Canon:**

 
 
• Also known as the Tipitaka, it is the canonical literature of Theravada Buddhism.
 
• The Tipitaka consists of three "baskets" (pitakas): the Vinaya Pitaka (monastic rules), the Sutta Pitaka (discourses), and the Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical and doctrinal analyses).
 
 
 
• **Dharma:**
 
 
• A key concept in Indian religions including Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Sikhism.
 
• In Buddhism, it refers to the teachings of the Buddha which lead to enlightenment.
 
 
 
• **Prakrit Languages:**
 
 
• A group of Middle Indo-Aryan languages, among which Pali is one.
 
• Prakrit languages were commonly spoken in ancient India and used in various Jain and Buddhist texts.
 
 
 
• **Tamil:**
 
 
• A Dravidian language spoken predominantly by the Tamil people of India and Sri Lanka.
 
• It is one of the oldest languages in the world with a rich literary tradition.
 
 
 
• **Abahatta:**
 
 
• A later form of Prakrit that evolved into the modern Indo-Aryan languages like Bengali, Assamese, and Oriya.
 
• It was spoken in eastern India during the medieval period.
